text: [serious] Here is Leah's same loan, started in April nineteen seventy-seven. It begins at seven point five percent, like every replay, and for a while her cushion grows. Then the Treasury bill rate climbs year after year, and her rate follows it, to nineteen point three percent at its highest. The cushion from her first months is soon gone, and every further month above nine percent adds to what she owes in interest. Her payment reaches eight hundred sixty-three dollars and thirty-six cents a month, against the fixed six hundred thirty-three dollars and thirty-eight cents. Over ten years, the fixed loan charges twenty-six thousand five dollars in interest. Leah's variable loan charges forty-three percent more interest than the fixed loan, the worst stretch in the whole replay. This replay has no rate cap; a real loan's cap, if low enough, would have made this worst case smaller.
